overview.summary: Officers of the Indian Administrative Service hold senior posts in central and state governments, running districts and departments and putting government policy into action. Roles vary with the posting.
overview.problems: They help make sure public services, such as land records, welfare schemes, elections and disaster relief, reach people fairly.
overview.worksWith: Elected leaders, police and other departments, local officials, citizens and community groups.
overview.workplaces: District offices, state secretariats, government departments and central ministries, with a lot of time in the field.

timeline.title: Reviewing files and plans
timeline.description: The officer reads reports, files and proposals that need decisions.
timeline.why: Decisions must follow the law and procedure.

timeline.title: Meeting citizens
timeline.description: The officer hears complaints and requests and directs action on them.

timeline.title: Reviews with departments
timeline.description: The officer checks the progress of schemes such as roads, schools or health programs with officials.

timeline.title: Field visits
timeline.description: The officer visits villages, offices, schools or projects to see conditions first-hand.

timeline.title: Meetings and orders
timeline.description: The officer drafts orders, answers queries from higher authorities and prepares for elections or events.
timeline.why: Written orders turn decisions into action.

timeline.title: Emergencies and elections
timeline.description: Floods and other disasters, or elections, require long hours and quick decisions.
timeline.why: Public services must keep working in a crisis.

responsibilities: Maintaining records and following the law
Reporting to elected leaders and senior officers
challenges: Selection is through a highly competitive national examination.
Hours are long and unpredictable, especially in emergencies and elections.
Pressure comes from many sides, including politics and public expectations.
Paperwork is heavy and rules are strict.
Decisions can have large consequences and receive public scrutiny.
Resources are limited compared with needs.
workEnvironment: Government offices and field locations, from city departments to rural districts. Time is divided between desk work, meetings and travel. Postings change every few years and may be in different states or remote areas.
rewards: A chance to improve public services at scale
Variety of roles over a career
Respect when public duty is done well

activity.title: Write a one-page note on a local civic problem
steps: Pick a safe, everyday problem such as litter near a school or a poorly lit road.
Observe it from a safe public place and note the facts.
Talk to two people who agree to share how it affects them.
List two possible solutions, who would need to act and what each might cost.
Write a one-page note recommending one option and naming one risk.
activity.outcome: You practise gathering facts, weighing options and writing a clear proposal, which administrators do every day.
activity.safety: Observe only from safe public places, do not photograph people, do not approach officials or anyone in a way that causes trouble, and ask an adult before sharing your note.

source: Written by Futurixia from general knowledge of how this profession works. It is illustrative and is not based on interviews or surveys.
